1	"""Write-ahead log key value store.
2	
3	Every mutation is first appended to a framed log. A commit marker is the
4	only thing that advances the durable sequence number. When a store is opened,
5	any tail that was never committed (including a record torn by a hard kill) is
6	discarded, so recovery always yields exactly the committed state.
7	
8	Only the very last log record may be incomplete: a process killed while
9	appending leaves at most one torn record, which is dropped without being
10	applied. Any other framing failure -- a truncated record in the middle, a
11	length field out of bounds, unparseable content, or a duplicate/regressing
12	commit sequence -- is corruption, and recovery raises ``CorruptLogError``
13	without touching the store.
14	
15	Recovery itself may be killed at any point, any number of times. Two small
16	sidecar files in the store directory, both maintained below the write path,
17	make the convergence protocol kill-safe and its report stable:
18	
19	``wal.ckp``
20	    A byte-for-byte copy of the log prefix ending at the most recent commit
21	    marker, replaced atomically (temp file, fsync, rename, directory fsync)
22	    only after that commit frame is durable. A log torn at *any* offset --
23	    even offset 0, or inside the committed prefix -- is rebuilt from it, so
24	    the durable sequence number never regresses. It is also the published
25	    snapshot read-only processes pin (see below).
26	
27	``wal.rec``
28	    A recovery marker written only after a log needing repair has passed
29	    full validation and only *before* the atomic rebuild starts. It records
30	    the clean prefix length and whether a torn record was discarded. Its
31	    presence makes a rebuild interrupted mid-copy converge on reopen (the
32	    rebuild is simply repeated) and keeps the reported ``discarded`` count
33	    stable across reopens and repeated recoveries. It is removed by the next
34	    successful commit.
35	
36	Range scans (``Store.scan(start, end)``) open an ordered read-only cursor
37	over the complete committed snapshot pinned at the moment the cursor is
38	opened. The cursor yields ``(key, value)`` pairs in bytewise key order --
39	keys compare by their raw UTF-8 bytes, with no encoding conversion -- from
40	``start`` (inclusive) to ``end`` (exclusive); a ``None`` endpoint leaves
41	that side unbounded. Keys that only ever appear in delete records never
42	show up, a key overwritten many times yields only its last committed value,
43	and empty values scan like any other. The snapshot is materialised once
44	when the cursor opens, so commits, compaction or crash recovery during the
45	scan never change it, reclaiming the old log space cannot break it, and the
46	cost of a scan is independent of how long the log's history is. A reversed
47	range (``start`` after ``end``) and any read from a closed cursor raise
48	``ValueError``.
49	
50	Read-only processes (``Store(path, read_only=True)``) take no lock and never
51	create or modify a file. At open each one picks the highest committed prefix
52	available at that instant -- the validated ``wal.log`` prefix or ``wal.ckp``
53	-- scans it once into memory and serves every ``get`` from that index.
54	Because the chosen image is complete and is only ever replaced atomically
55	(never edited in place), a refresh caught mid-rename, a half-written commit,
56	a torn record, or a log being rebuilt, shrunk or compacted can never expose
57	partial bytes: each read lands on one full committed snapshot that was
58	current at or after the open. A directory written by an older version is
59	opened the same way from its log and checkpoint. Reads never replay the log
60	afterwards, so their cost is independent of history and they never block
61	the writer; a reader that is killed or simply hangs changes nothing on disk.
62	
63	Compaction (``Store.compact()``) rewrites the committed history into one
64	tight image without losing a byte of committed state. The compacted log
65	holds exactly the live puts -- one per currently committed key, in sorted
66	key order -- followed by a *base commit* marker carrying the pre-compaction
67	sequence number. The durable sequence keeps that value, so the next commit
68	is ``seq + 1`` and every later commit continues the strict sequence; keys
69	that were deleted never come back. The image is assembled in memory and
70	staged as the atomically replaced ``wal.cmp`` sidecar; finishing installs
71	it as ``wal.ckp`` first and as ``wal.log`` second. Every intermediate state
72	is therefore either the pair of old files or the pair of complete new
73	images, which is precisely the two-image world the reader already chooses
74	between: a kill anywhere leaves a state reopening converges by simply
75	repeating the finish, and interrupting compaction any number of times
76	produces the same bytes as one clean run. Live readers keep serving their
77	pinned old snapshots (the inode survives on Unix; on Windows readers hold
78	no writer-side fd) and new readers land on the new snapshot, never a mix,
79	a half-written file or a byte that was already reclaimed.
80	
81	The durable commit boundary is the highest of the validated log boundary,
82	the checkpoint boundary and the marker boundary, so it can never move
83	backwards. Every repair step is either idempotent or an atomic rename; a
84	kill between any two steps leaves a state the next open converges from to
85	the identical result.
86	
87	Log frame layout (all integers big-endian)::
88	
89	    +---------+----------------+------------+----------------------+---------+
90	    | b"WAL2" | payload_length | header_crc | payload              | crc32   |
91	    | 4 bytes | 8 bytes        | 4 bytes    | metadata\\n<value>    | 4 bytes |
92	    +---------+----------------+------------+----------------------+---------+
93	
94	``header_crc`` is the crc32 of the magic and length bytes. It makes a
95	partial header that borrows bytes from a following frame fail validation,
96	so an incomplete record in the middle of the log reads as corruption while
97	a genuinely short final header reads as a torn tail.
98	
99	Metadata is a compact JSON object: ``{"t":"p","k":key}`` for puts,
100	``{"t":"d","k":key}`` for deletes, ``{"t":"c","s":seq}`` for ordinary
101	commits and ``{"t":"b","s":seq}`` for the base commit that closes a
102	compacted log. The two carry the sequence identically; a base marker is
103	additionally required to be the first commit marker in its file.
104	The raw value bytes follow the first newline, so values need no encoding.
105	"""
106	
107	from __future__ import annotations
108	
109	import io
110	import json
111	import os
112	import sys
113	import zlib
114	
115	__all__ = ["Store", "ScanCursor", "CorruptLogError", "inject_tear"]
116	
117	
118	class CorruptLogError(ValueError):
119	    """The write-ahead log is corrupt, not merely missing a torn tail.
120	
121	    A single incomplete final record is a normal crash remnant and is
122	    discarded during recovery. Anything else that fails framing, checksum,
123	    metadata or commit-sequence validation is corruption; recovery stops
124	    without applying or removing anything.
125	    """
126	
127	
128	class ScanCursor:
129	    """Ordered read-only cursor over one pinned committed snapshot.
130	
131	    Created by :meth:`Store.scan`. Iterating yields ``(key, value)`` pairs
132	    in bytewise key order -- keys ordered by their raw UTF-8 bytes, values
133	    returned as the exact stored bytes -- covering the range given at open:
134	    the start key inclusive, the end key exclusive, either side unbounded
135	    when its endpoint was ``None``.
136	
137	    The snapshot is fully materialised when the cursor opens, so later
138	    commits, compaction, crash recovery or reclamation of the old log space
139	    never change what the cursor yields, and closing the store it came from
140	    does not disturb it. The cursor is an iterator; it is also a context
141	    manager, and ``close()`` releases the snapshot early. Reading from a
142	    closed cursor raises ``ValueError``.
143	    """
144	
145	    def __init__(self, items):
146	        # ``items`` is the materialised snapshot: (key, value) pairs already
147	        # sorted by the keys' raw UTF-8 bytes and clipped to the range.
148	        self._items = items
149	        self._pos = 0
150	        self._closed = False
151	
152	    def __iter__(self) -> "ScanCursor":
153	        return self
154	
155	    def __next__(self):
156	        if self._closed:
157	            raise ValueError("scan cursor is closed")
158	        if self._pos >= len(self._items):
159	            raise StopIteration
160	        item = self._items[self._pos]
161	        self._pos += 1
162	        return item
163	
164	    @property
165	    def closed(self) -> bool:
166	        return self._closed
167	
168	    def close(self) -> None:
169	        self._items = []
170	        self._closed = True
171	
172	    def __enter__(self) -> "ScanCursor":
173	        return self
174	
175	    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb) -> None:
176	        self.close()
177	
178	
179	LOG_NAME = "wal.log"
180	_CHECKPOINT_NAME = "wal.ckp"
181	_MARKER_NAME = "wal.rec"
182	_COMPACT_NAME = "wal.cmp"
183	
184	_MAGIC = b"WAL2"
185	_PREFIX = 12  # 4 bytes magic + 8 bytes payload length
186	_HEADER = 16   # prefix + 4 bytes crc32 of the prefix
187	_TRAILER = 4   # crc32 of the payload
188	_MAX_PAYLOAD = 1 << 40
189	
190	_OP_PUT = "p"
191	_OP_DELETE = "d"
192	_OP_COMMIT = "c"
193	_OP_BASE = "b"
194	_COMMIT_OPS = (_OP_COMMIT, _OP_BASE)
195	
196	# os.open defaults to the C runtime's text mode on Windows, which would
197	# expand every "\n" to "\r\n" inside os.write and inflate the log on disk.
198	# Forcing binary keeps the log bytes identical on every platform; the flag
199	# does not exist elsewhere, where it is 0.
200	_O_BINARY = getattr(os, "O_BINARY", 0)
201	
202	
203	def _encode_frame(op: str, value: bytes = b"", key: str | None = None,
204	                  seq: int | None = None) -> bytes:
205	    meta: dict[str, object] = {"t": op}
206	    if key is not None:
207	        meta["k"] = key
208	    if seq is not None:
209	        meta["s"] = seq
210	    head = json.dumps(meta, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")
211	    payload = head + b"\n" + value
212	    prefix = _MAGIC + len(payload).to_bytes(8, "big")
213	    header = prefix + zlib.crc32(prefix).to_bytes(4, "big")
214	    return header + payload + zlib.crc32(payload).to_bytes(4, "big")
215	
216	
217	def _iter_frames(f):
218	    """Scan an open binary log file from position 0.
219	
220	    For every intact frame yields
221	    ``("frame", meta, value, start, end)``. Scanning stops with either no
222	    terminal event (clean EOF), ``("torn", start)`` for a single incomplete
223	    final frame, or ``("invalid", start)`` for a frame that fails framing,
224	    header/payload checksum or metadata parsing. With the header checksum a
225	    partial header that borrows bytes from a following record cannot survive,
226	    so a short read landing exactly at EOF is reliably the one unfinished
227	    record a single writer was appending when it died; bytes left beyond such
228	    a read instead make it corruption.
229	    """
230	    f.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)
231	    eof = f.tell()
232	    f.seek(0)
233	    while True:
234	        start = f.tell()
235	        header = f.read(_HEADER)
236	        if not header:
237	            return
238	        if len(header) < _HEADER:
239	            # Trailing bytes of a frame header are a torn tail only when
240	            # nothing follows them; a gap anywhere else is corruption.
241	            yield (("torn", start) if f.tell() == eof
242	                   else ("invalid", start))
243	            return
244	        if header[:4] != _MAGIC:
245	            yield "invalid", start
246	            return
247	        if int.from_bytes(header[_PREFIX:], "big") != zlib.crc32(
248	                header[:_PREFIX]):
249	            yield "invalid", start
250	            return
251	        length = int.from_bytes(header[4:_PREFIX], "big")
252	        if length > _MAX_PAYLOAD:
253	            yield "invalid", start
254	            return
255	        payload = f.read(length)
256	        checksum = f.read(_TRAILER)
257	        if len(payload) < length or len(checksum) < _TRAILER:
258	            # Only the single final record may be incomplete.
259	            yield (("torn", start) if f.tell() == eof
260	                   else ("invalid", start))

262	        if int.from_bytes(checksum, "big") != zlib.crc32(payload):
263	            yield "invalid", start
264	            return
265	        newline = payload.find(b"\n")
266	        if newline < 0:
267	            yield "invalid", start
268	            return
269	        try:
270	            meta = json.loads(payload[:newline])
271	        except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError):
272	            yield "invalid", start
273	            return
274	        if not isinstance(meta, dict) or not isinstance(meta.get("t"), str):
275	            yield "invalid", start
276	            return
277	        yield "frame", meta, payload[newline + 1:], start, f.tell()

284	    (access denied); directory entries there are made durable by the file's

286	    working everywhere. Other platforms occasionally refuse the directory
287	    open or the fsync the same way (restrictive mounts, virtualised FSes);
288	    that is likewise best-effort -- the file's own fsync is what carries the

290	    creation or a commit/compaction.

299	        try:
300	            os.fsync(fd)
301	        except PermissionError:
302	            # Some non-Windows mounts reject directory fsync the same way.
303	            pass

314	def inject_tear(source, destination, offset):
315	    """Copy a log cut at exactly ``offset`` bytes, for bytewise verification.
316	
317	    Produces ``destination`` containing the first ``offset`` bytes of
318	    ``source`` -- a replica of a process killed precisely when the write had
319	    reached that byte offset. The source file is never modified. Either path
320	    argument may be a store directory, in which case its ``wal.log`` is used.
321	
322	    ``offset`` must satisfy ``0 <= offset <= len(source)``; a negative or
323	    past-the-end offset raises ``IndexError``. The full-length copy
324	    (``offset == len(source)``) is the clean control case.
325	
326	    Verification aid only; the normal write path never calls this.
327	    """
328	    if not isinstance(offset, int) or isinstance(offset, bool):
329	        raise TypeError("offset must be an integer byte offset")
330	
331	    src = os.path.join(source, LOG_NAME) if os.path.isdir(source) else source
332	    dst = (os.path.join(destination, LOG_NAME)
333	           if os.path.isdir(destination) else destination)
334	
335	    size = os.path.getsize(src)
336	    if offset < 0 or offset > size:
337	        raise IndexError(
338	            f"tear offset {offset} out of range for log of {size} bytes")
339	    if os.path.abspath(src) == os.path.abspath(dst):
340	        raise ValueError("tear destination must differ from the source log")
341	
342	    remaining = offset
343	    with open(src, "rb") as fsrc, open(dst, "wb") as fdst:
344	        while remaining:
345	            chunk = fsrc.read(min(remaining, 1 << 20))
346	            if not chunk:  # pragma: no cover - size came from the same file
347	                raise IndexError("source log shrank while copying")
348	            fdst.write(chunk)
349	            remaining -= len(chunk)
350	        fdst.truncate(offset)
351	        os.fsync(fdst.fileno())
352	    return dst

355	class Store:
356	    """A single-writer key value store backed by an append-only log.
357	
358	    ``path`` must be an existing store directory; the log file inside it is
359	    created on first use. Opening a missing directory raises
360	    ``FileNotFoundError`` and opening a path that is not a directory raises
361	    ``OSError``.
362	
363	    With ``read_only=True`` the store is opened purely for reading. No file
364	    is ever created or modified, and no lock is taken: any number of
365	    read-only processes may coexist with the one writer. The reader pins the
366	    committed snapshot current at open time -- the highest committed prefix
367	    of ``wal.log`` or of the atomically replaced ``wal.ckp`` sidecar --
368	    scans it once, and serves every ``get`` from that in-memory index. The
369	    snapshot is independent of the log's later history, so a read never
370	    replays the log and cannot block the writer, and uncommitted bytes, a
371	    half-written commit, a torn record or a half-finished rebuild are never
372	    visible. ``put``, ``delete``, ``commit``, ``recover`` and ``compact``
373	    are rejected on a read-only store; ``stats`` reports the pinned
374	    snapshot.
375	
376	    ``scan(start, end)`` -- on either open form -- returns a
377	    :class:`ScanCursor` over the complete committed snapshot pinned at the
378	    moment of the call, yielding ``(key, value)`` pairs in bytewise key
379	    order from ``start`` (inclusive) to ``end`` (exclusive); a ``None``
380	    endpoint leaves that side unbounded. Uncommitted session changes of a
381	    writer are not part of the snapshot. The cursor reads from memory only:
382	    it never touches the log, takes no lock, and is unaffected by later
383	    commits, compaction, recovery or the store closing.
384	    """
385	
386	    def __init__(self, path: str, read_only: bool = False):
387	        self._dir = path
388	        self._path = os.path.join(path, LOG_NAME)
389	        self._ckp_path = os.path.join(path, _CHECKPOINT_NAME)
390	        self._marker_path = os.path.join(path, _MARKER_NAME)
391	        self._cmp_path = os.path.join(path, _COMPACT_NAME)
392	        self._read_only = read_only
393	
394	        # Recovery needs a directory to replay; a missing target is an error
395	        # at open time, not an implicit create.
396	        if not os.path.exists(path):
397	            raise FileNotFoundError(
398	                f"store directory does not exist: {path!r}")
399	        if not os.path.isdir(path):
400	            raise OSError(f"store path is not a directory: {path!r}")
401	
402	        self._data: dict[str, bytes] = {}
403	        self._seq = 0
404	        self._entries = 0
405	        self._pending = 0
406	        self._closed = False
407	        self._corrupt = False
408	        # Committed value of each key this session has touched since the
409	        # last commit (None when the key was absent); lets a scan pin the
410	        # committed snapshot without replaying the log.
411	        self._touched: dict[str, bytes | None] = {}
412	        # Torn records dropped in this recovery epoch; wal.rec carries it
413	        # across processes until the next commit.
414	        self._discarded = 0
415	
416	        if read_only:
417	            # A read-only open holds no writable fd and never takes a lock;
418	            # leave the writer fd slot unset for clarity.
419	            self._fd = -1
420	            self._open_read_only()
421	            return
422	
423	        log_created = not os.path.exists(self._path)
424	        self._fd = os.open(self._path,
425	                           os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND | _O_BINARY,
426	                           0o644)
427	        if log_created:
428	            os.fsync(self._fd)
429	            _fsync_dir(path)

431	        self._converge_on_open()

433	    # -- log scanning and validation --------------------------------------
434	
435	    def _read_log(self, path=None):
436	        frames = []
437	        terminal = None
438	        with open(path or self._path, "rb") as f:
439	            for event in _iter_frames(f):
440	                if event[0] == "frame":
441	                    _, meta, value, start, end = event
442	                    frames.append((meta, value, start, end))
443	                else:
444	                    terminal = event
445	        return frames, terminal
446	
447	    @staticmethod
448	    def _validate(frames, terminal):
449	        """Validate every frame and the strictly increasing commit sequence.
450	
451	        Returns ``(committed_end, last_seq)`` -- the byte offset just past
452	        the last commit marker and its sequence number. An ``"invalid"``
453	        terminal is corruption and raises ``CorruptLogError``; a ``"torn"``
454	        terminal is left for the caller, which decides from the durable
455	        checkpoint whether it is a tail to discard or a gash to restore.
456	
457	        A compacted image starts with a base commit marker (``"b"``) that
458	        carries the pre-compaction sequence: it must be the first commit
459	        marker in the file, it establishes the expected sequence at
460	        ``seq + 1`` and no second base marker may ever follow. An ordinary
461	        first commit must still be sequence 1.
462	        """
463	        expected_seq = 1
464	        last_seq = 0
465	        committed_end = 0
466	        for meta, _value, _start, end in frames:
467	            op = meta.get("t")
468	            if op in (_OP_PUT, _OP_DELETE):
469	                key = meta.get("k")
470	                if not isinstance(key, str) or key == "":
471	                    raise CorruptLogError(
472	                        f"invalid frame metadata: {meta!r}")
473	            elif op == _OP_BASE:
474	                seq = meta.get("s")
475	                if not isinstance(seq, int) or isinstance(seq, bool):
476	                    raise CorruptLogError(
477	                        f"invalid base commit marker: {meta!r}")
478	                if last_seq != 0:
479	                    raise CorruptLogError(
480	                        "base commit must be the first commit marker")
481	                if seq < 1:
482	                    raise CorruptLogError(
483	                        f"base commit sequence {seq} out of order")
484	                last_seq = seq
485	                expected_seq = seq + 1
486	                committed_end = end
487	            elif op == _OP_COMMIT:
488	                seq = meta.get("s")
489	                if not isinstance(seq, int) or isinstance(seq, bool):
490	                    raise CorruptLogError(
491	                        f"invalid commit marker: {meta!r}")
492	                if seq != expected_seq:
493	                    raise CorruptLogError(
494	                        f"commit sequence {seq} out of order, "
495	                        f"expected {expected_seq}")
496	                last_seq = seq
497	                expected_seq += 1
498	                committed_end = end
499	            else:
500	                raise CorruptLogError(f"unknown frame type: {op!r}")
501	        if terminal is not None and terminal[0] == "invalid":
502	            raise CorruptLogError("corrupt log frame")
503	        return committed_end, last_seq

505	    @staticmethod
506	    def _replay(frames) -> tuple[dict[str, bytes], int]:
507	        state: dict[str, bytes] = {}
508	        applied = 0
509	        for meta, value, _start, _end in frames:
510	            op = meta["t"]
511	            if op in _COMMIT_OPS:
512	                continue
513	            if op == _OP_PUT:
514	                state[meta["k"]] = value
515	            else:  # _OP_DELETE
516	                state.pop(meta["k"], None)
517	            applied += 1

626	    def _rebuild_log(self, clean_end: int) -> None:
627	        """Make the log exactly its clean ``[0, clean_end)`` prefix.
628	
629	        Kill-safe and idempotent: when a checkpoint covers the prefix the new
630	        log is fully written and fsynced as a temp file and atomically renamed
631	        over the old one, so a kill leaves either the old log or the complete
632	        restored log -- never a half-written file -- and rerunning converges.
633	        Without a checkpoint but with the committed bytes still at stable
634	        offsets, a synced truncate drops the tail instead. The empty prefix is
635	        a truncate to zero.
636	        """
637	        size = os.fstat(self._fd).st_size
638	        if size == clean_end:
639	            return
640	
641	        if clean_end == 0:
642	            os.ftruncate(self._fd, 0)
643	            os.fsync(self._fd)
644	            return
645	
646	        try:
647	            ckp_size = os.path.getsize(self._ckp_path)
648	        except FileNotFoundError:
649	            ckp_size = -1
650	
651	        if ckp_size < clean_end and size > clean_end:
652	            # No checkpoint, but the committed bytes survive at stable
653	            # offsets: drop the dirty tail. Idempotent if killed mid-call.
654	            try:
655	                os.fsync(self._fd)
656	            except OSError:
657	                pass
658	            os.ftruncate(self._fd, clean_end)
659	            os.fsync(self._fd)
660	            return
661	        if ckp_size < clean_end:
662	            raise CorruptLogError(
663	                "committed prefix is torn and no checkpoint covers it")
664	
665	        tmp = self._path + ".tmp"
666	        with open(self._ckp_path, "rb") as fsrc, open(tmp, "wb") as fdst:
667	            self._copy_prefix(fsrc, fdst, clean_end)
668	            os.fsync(fdst.fileno())

670	        os.close(self._fd)
671	        try:
672	            os.replace(tmp, self._path)
673	            _fsync_dir(self._dir)

675	            self._fd = os.open(
676	                self._path,
677	                os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND | _O_BINARY, 0o644)

683	    def _build_compact_image(self, seq: int) -> tuple[bytes, int]:
684	        """Serialise the committed state into one compact log image.
685	
686	        One put frame per live key, keys in sorted order, followed by a base
687	        commit marker carrying the pre-compaction sequence. The empty state
688	        at seq 0 is an empty image rather than a zero-sequence marker.
689	        """
690	        if seq == 0:
691	            return b"", 0
692	        parts = [_encode_frame(_OP_PUT, value, key=key)
693	                 for key, value in sorted(self._data.items())]
694	        parts.append(_encode_frame(_OP_BASE, seq=seq))
695	        return b"".join(parts), len(self._data)

697	    def _read_compact_candidate(self):

699	
700	        Returns ``(image, end, seq, live)`` where ``image`` is the exact
701	        byte content, or ``None`` when the sidecar is absent. The image must
702	        be a clean file ending exactly on a base commit marker, preceded only
703	        by put frames with strictly increasing keys; anything else is
704	        corruption of the crash-convergence machinery, never a discardable
705	        tail (the sidecar is always atomically replaced, never written in
706	        place).
707	        """
708	        try:
709	            f = open(self._cmp_path, "rb")
710	        except FileNotFoundError:
711	            return None
712	        with f:
713	            image = f.read()
714	        if not image:
715	            # An empty candidate encodes the empty state at seq 0.
716	            return b"", 0, 0, 0
717	
718	        frames, terminal = self._scan_bytes(image)
719	        if terminal is not None:
720	            raise CorruptLogError(
721	                "compaction candidate is not a clean committed prefix")
722	        end, seq = self._validate(frames, None)
723	        if end != len(image) or seq <= 0:
724	            raise CorruptLogError(
725	                "compaction candidate has bytes past its base commit")
726	        live = 0
727	        last_key: str | None = None
728	        saw_base = False
729	        for meta, _value, _start, _end in frames:
730	            op = meta.get("t")
731	            if op == _OP_PUT:
732	                if saw_base:
733	                    raise CorruptLogError(
734	                        "compaction candidate has puts past its base commit")

736	                if last_key is not None and key <= last_key:
737	                    raise CorruptLogError(
738	                        "compaction candidate keys are not sorted uniquely")

740	                live += 1
741	            elif op == _OP_BASE:
742	                if saw_base:
743	                    raise CorruptLogError(
744	                        "compaction candidate has multiple base commits")
745	                saw_base = True

748	                    "compaction candidate contains a non-compacted frame")

751	                "compaction candidate ends without a base commit")

771	        kill leaves either the old log or the complete new one -- never a
772	        half-written log. The append fd is closed for the rename because
773	        Windows cannot replace a path held open by it, then reopened.
774	        """
775	        tmp = self._path + ".tmp"

791	    def _install_compaction(self, image: bytes, seq: int) -> None:

796	        replaced next and the log last, both via complete-file atomic
797	        renames, then the candidate is removed. Any ordering of a kill
798	        between those steps leaves the durable files equal to either the old
799	        pair or the complete new pair, and rerunning (via the surviving
800	        candidate) converges to the same compacted bytes.
801	        """
802	        # Compaction closes any prior recovery epoch the way a commit does;
803	        # do it while the old log still exists so a later kill replays this
804	        # whole publish from the durable candidate.
805	        self._remove_marker()
806	
807	        if seq == 0:
808	            # Empty committed state: the log is zero length and there is no
809	            # checkpoint to publish; reclaim every old byte and drop the plan.
810	            os.ftruncate(self._fd, 0)
811	            os.fsync(self._fd)
812	            try:
813	                os.unlink(self._ckp_path)
814	                _fsync_dir(self._dir)
815	            except FileNotFoundError:
816	                pass
817	            self._remove_candidate()
818	            return

820	        def write(fdst):
821	            fdst.write(image)
822	
823	        self._atomic_file(self._ckp_path, write)
824	        self._install_log_bytes(image)
825	        self._remove_candidate()

840	        whose boundary a newer durable epoch has overtaken is stale and is
841	        discarded instead.

871	        never regress. A log torn inside its committed prefix is rebuilt from
